module.title: Consumer Rights, Product Warranties & Constructive Assertiveness
module.objective: Menyampaikan keluhan konsumen secara tegas, sopan, dan efektif untuk menuntut pengembalian dana atau penggantian barang rusak.

subModules.title: Reading Mission: Consumer Rights, Product Warranties & Constructive Assertiveness
subModules.grammarFocus: Assertive phrasing with 'I am entitled to...', 'I insist on...', and Present Perfect for ongoing issues
subModules.vocabularyFocus: Consumer rights, warranties, defects, and polite escalation terms

content.summary: In this reading mission, you will explore how consumers can handle faulty products and speak up effectively. You will read realistic dialogues and formal emails where shoppers demand refunds, explain warranty terms, and remain polite yet firm.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Using legal rights phrases (I am entitled to), strong demands (I insist on), and the present perfect for unresolved problems.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Essential terms related to warranties, defects, specifications, and customer protection.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Skimming for the main purpose of a complaint and scanning for specific product details and warranty conditions.

learningObjectives: Understand the main purpose of formal consumer complaint texts and emails.
Locate specific product details, defect descriptions, and warranty timelines.
Recognize and apply constructive assertiveness grammar patterns.

contextWarmup.prompt: What is the best way to act when you buy a brand new electronic device and it breaks down the very next day?
options: Contact the store politely, state the problem clearly, and show your receipt to request a replacement.
Throw the item away immediately and never buy anything from that store again.
Shout at the cashier until they give you all your money back plus extra cash.
contextWarmup.explanation: Being polite, clear, and organized with your receipt and warranty details is the most effective way to resolve consumer issues.

rules: Gunakan 'I am entitled to...' untuk merujuk hak konsumen: 'I am entitled to a full refund under the Consumer Protection Act' atau 'I am entitled to a replacement within the warranty period'.

Gunakan 'The product is defective/faulty' untuk menjelaskan masalah: 'The product is defective and does not match the specifications stated on the box' atau 'The item is faulty and stopped working after two days'.

Gunakan 'I insist on...' atau 'I must insist that...' untuk menekankan permintaan: 'I insist on speaking with a customer relations supervisor' atau 'I must insist that you process my refund immediately'.
Gunakan present perfect untuk menggambarkan masalah berkelanjutan: 'I have contacted your support team three times' atau 'The issue has not been resolved despite my multiple complaints'.

commonTrap.trapTitle: Being Too Aggressive or Too Passive
commonTrap.explanation: Learners often think they have to shout to be heard, or they are too shy to ask for a refund. Constructive assertiveness means staying calm, polite, and firm using specific facts.
commonTrap.wrong: Give me my money back right now, your shop is terrible!
commonTrap.correct: I am returning this faulty item and I am entitled to a full refund under the store warranty policy.

content.passageTitle: Knowing Your Rights at the Return Counter
paragraphs: Last Saturday, Sarah walked into TechWorld Electronics with a serious expression and a receipt in her hand. Two days earlier, she had purchased a new smartphone, but the device proved to be completely defective. Whenever she tried to open the camera application, the screen froze and turned black. Instead of getting angry or shouting at the staff, Sarah practiced constructive assertiveness. She approached the customer service desk with a calm tone and clear facts.

When the store assistant looked at the phone and suggested sending it away for a three-week repair, Sarah politely stood her ground. She explained that under consumer protection laws, she was entitled to an immediate replacement because the item was faulty upon arrival. She stated clearly that the phone did not meet the advertised specifications. Realizing that Sarah knew her rights and spoke with confidence, the assistant checked the inventory and immediately processed a brand new replacement unit for her.

subModules.title: Listening Mission: Returning a Faulty Product

content.summary: Listen for specific details such as time periods, model names, and store policies when making a return. Pay close attention to how speakers use firm tone and polite language to assert their consumer rights.
learningObjectives: Catch the main topic of a spoken conversation about product returns.
Identify details such as receipts, warranties, and store policies.
Notice how words link together in connected speech during polite complaints.

keyPhrases.note: Used to describe an item that does not work correctly because of a manufacturing defect.
Asking to get all your money back after returning a broken item.
Legal rules protecting buyers from unfair business practices.
Document proving the guarantee terms provided by the manufacturer.

connectedSpeech.note: The final /t/ sound in stopped blends directly into the /w/ sound of working.
The plural /s/ in weeks links smoothly to the vowel sound in ago.
The dark /l/ at the end of full connects naturally with the start of refund.
The /t/ in just and the article a weaken into a continuous rhythm.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Assertive Consumer Communication and Warranty Claims

content.summary: This guide covers how to write formal, assertive emails and letters regarding consumer rights, product warranties, and return requests. You will learn how to state complaints clearly, quote legal entitlements, and demand prompt resolutions politely yet firmly.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Stating the Product Problem Clearly
blueprintItems.formula: The [product name] + is defective / faulty + because + [specific issue].
blueprintItems.example: The wireless headphone is defective because the left speaker stopped working after two days.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Claiming Legal Entitlements
blueprintItems.formula: I am entitled to + [noun phrase / full refund / replacement] + under + [warranty / consumer act].
blueprintItems.example: I am entitled to a full refund under the Consumer Protection Act.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Making Firm Demands and Next Steps
blueprintItems.example: I insist on receiving a replacement unit by Friday or escalating this matter to the consumer bureau.

mechanicsRules.rule: Always capitalize proper business names, legal acts, and days of the week.
mechanicsRules.badExample: i contacted consumer protection act on monday.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: I contacted the Consumer Protection Act office on Monday.
mechanicsRules.why: Specific legal acts, days, and starting words require capital letters in formal English writing.

mechanicsRules.rule: Avoid exclamation marks in formal complaint letters.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: This product fails to meet acceptable quality standards.
mechanicsRules.why: Formal complaints achieve better results through objective, calm language rather than emotional punctuation.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use commas correctly after introductory prepositional phrases in formal correspondence.
mechanicsRules.badExample: On arrival at my home the television failed to turn on.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: On arrival at my home, the television failed to turn on.
mechanicsRules.why: Introductory phrases longer than four words need a comma to separate them from the main clause.

sampleSentences.en: I am writing to express my dissatisfaction with a faulty smartphone I purchased last week.
sampleSentences.id: Saya menulis untuk menyatakan ketidakpuasan saya terhadap ponsel pintar rusak yang saya beli minggu lalu.
sampleSentences.focus: Formal complaint opening and adjective choice

sampleSentences.en: The item is defective and does not match the specifications stated on the official box.
sampleSentences.id: Barang tersebut cacat dan tidak sesuai dengan spesifikasi yang tertera di kotak resmi.

sampleSentences.en: I have contacted your customer support team three times without receiving any helpful response.
sampleSentences.id: Saya telah menghubungi tim dukungan pelanggan Anda tiga kali tanpa menerima tanggapan yang membantu.
sampleSentences.focus: Using present perfect for ongoing unresolved issues

sampleSentences.en: I must insist that you process my refund immediately to avoid further formal action.
sampleSentences.id: Saya harus bersikeras agar Anda segera memproses pengembalian dana saya untuk menghindari tindakan resmi lebih lanjut.

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 1: Describe a Faulty Appliance
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write three sentences describing a kitchen appliance you bought that broke down quickly. State when you bought it, what went wrong, and what you expect the store to do.
guidedLabChallenges.example: I purchased a coffee machine last month from your store. Unfortunately, the heating element is faulty and burned out yesterday. I expect a full refund or a working replacement by this weekend.

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 2: Assertive Customer Email
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write an assertive follow-up message about an unresolved complaint. Mention that you have contacted support multiple times and insist on immediate action.
guidedLabChallenges.example: I have contacted your support team three times regarding my broken laptop. The issue has not been resolved despite my multiple complaints. I must insist that you process my refund immediately.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change the following affirmative sentence into a complete negative sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Luke enjoys playing video games after dinner.
targetAnswers: Luke doesn't enjoy playing video games after dinner.
Luke does not enjoy playing video games after dinner.
practicumQuestions.explanation: With third-person singular (Luke), use 'does not' or 'doesn't' followed by the base verb 'enjoy'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine the two sentences using the conjunction 'because':
practicumQuestions.promptText: The laptop stopped working after two days. The hard drive was defective.
practicumQuestions.hint: Place 'because' between the main clause and the reason.
targetAnswers: The laptop stopped working after two days because the hard drive was defective.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The conjunction 'because' connects the result to its direct cause smoothly.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the following sentence with correct capitalization and punctuation:
practicumQuestions.promptText: i bought a faulty television at sony store on friday.
practicumQuestions.hint: Capitalize the pronoun, proper brand name, and day of the week.
targetAnswers: I bought a faulty television at Sony Store on Friday.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Pronouns ('I'), company names ('Sony Store'), and days ('Friday') must always be capitalized.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write a sentence stating your legal right to a refund using the exact phrase 'I am entitled to':
practicumQuestions.promptText: State your right to a refund for a broken watch under consumer law.
practicumQuestions.hint: Start with 'I am entitled to a full refund...'
targetAnswers: I am entitled to a full refund under consumer law.
I am entitled to a full refund under the Consumer Protection Act.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Using 'I am entitled to' clearly establishes legal consumer rights in formal complaints.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Transform this statement into a polite but firm insistence using 'I insist on':
practicumQuestions.promptText: You need to give me my money back right now.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'I insist on receiving...' or 'I insist on getting...'
targetAnswers: I insist on receiving my money back immediately.
I insist on getting my money back immediately.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The phrase 'I insist on' followed by a gerund (-ing verb) conveys constructive assertiveness.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence using the present perfect tense to show an ongoing complaint:
practicumQuestions.promptText: I contact your support team three times.
targetAnswers: I have contacted your support team three times.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The present perfect ('have contacted') highlights actions that connect the past to the present moment.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the punctuation and capitalization errors in this sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: the product is defective therefore i want a replacement.
practicumQuestions.hint: Add a semicolon or period before 'therefore', or use a comma with a conjunction.
targetAnswers: The product is defective; therefore, I want a replacement.
The product is defective, so I want a replacement.
The product is defective. Therefore, I want a replacement.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Conjunctive adverbs like 'therefore' require proper punctuation such as a semicolon or a separate sentence.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write a sentence explaining that an item does not match expectations using 'does not match':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Describe a dress that looks different from the online picture.
targetAnswers: The dress does not match the picture online.
The item does not match the description on your website.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Stating that an item 'does not match' is a standard consumer rights argument for returns.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change this direct order into a polite formal sentence using 'I must insist that':
practicumQuestions.promptText: You must process my refund immediately.
practicumQuestions.hint: Start with 'I must insist that you...'
targetAnswers: I must insist that you process my refund immediately.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Starting with 'I must insist that' makes demands sound professional and formal rather than aggressive.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write a complete sentence describing a faulty product using the word 'faulty':
practicumQuestions.promptText: State that a toaster is broken and dangerous.
targetAnswers: The toaster is faulty and dangerous to use.
The toaster is faulty and stopped working.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Describing an item as 'faulty' clearly signals a warranty claim or product defect.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Consumer Rights, Product Warranties & Constructive Assertiveness

content.summary: Mastering constructive assertiveness in English requires clear articulation, polite intonation, and steady pacing when demanding refunds or replacements for faulty items.
content.audioGuidance: Maintain a firm yet polite tone. Use falling intonation when stating facts and polite rising intonation when asking for managerial intervention.

pillars.name: Consonant Clarity
pillars.target: Precise articulation of plosives in technical terms
pillars.explanation: Clear pronunciation of the /t/ and /d/ sounds in words like defective, refund, and faulty ensures your complaint is understood without ambiguity.

pillars.name: Assertive Intonation
pillars.target: Controlled vocal projection for formal complaints
pillars.explanation: Avoid aggressive shouting or hesitant mumbling. Speak with a steady volume and measured tempo to sound professional and legally informed.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Notice how the primary stress shifts from the second syllable in the adjective to the third syllable in the derived noun form.
The noun warranty places stress on the first syllable, whereas the person receiving the warranty shifts the stress to the final syllable.
The verb escalate has stress on the first syllable, while the noun escalation shifts the main stress to the third syllable.
The verb specify stresses the first syllable, whereas the long noun specification places its primary stress on the fourth syllable.

drills.focus: Clear plosives and precise vowel sounds in complaint context

drills.focus: Linking words smoothly in legal rights statements

drills.hint: Raise your pitch slightly on 'escalate' to show firm resolve.

roleplay.context: You are standing at the customer service desk of an electronics store, returning a faulty tablet.

turns.speaker: Store Clerk
turns.text: Good afternoon. How can I help you with your purchase today?
turns.translation: Selamat siang. Bagaimana saya bisa membantu pembelian Anda hari ini?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Good afternoon. I bought this tablet yesterday, but it is defective.
turns.translation: Selamat siang. Saya membeli tablet ini kemarin, tetapi perangkat ini rusak.

turns.speaker: Store Clerk
turns.text: I am sorry to hear that. Do you have the receipt and original box?
turns.translation: Saya turut menyesal mendengarnya. Apakah Anda membawa nota dan kotak aslinya?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yes, I have both right here. I am entitled to a replacement under warranty.
turns.translation: Ya, saya bawa keduanya di sini. Saya berhak mendapatkan penggantian berdasarkan garansi.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 20 seconds about a time you bought a product that turned out to be faulty.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Describe an experience when you purchased a defective item and how you handled the situation.
storyPoints: What product you bought and where you purchased it from
What specific problem or defect you discovered after opening it
How you returned to the store and what resolution you demanded
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: I bought a coffee maker last week, but it was defective so I returned it for a full refund.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /aɪ bɔːt ə ˈkɒfi ˈmeɪkə lɑːst wiːk, bʌt ɪt wɒz dɪˈfektɪv səʊ aɪ rɪˈtɜːnd ɪt fɔː ə fʊl ˈriːfʌnd/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Tell your story using past tense verbs and connectives clearly.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 20 seconds about why understanding consumer rights is important.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Explain why every customer should know their warranty rights and protection laws.
storyPoints: A common situation where unknowledgeable buyers lose money on broken goods
How knowing consumer protection laws empowers you to speak up
What action you take when a seller refuses to cooperate initially
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Knowing consumer protection laws ensures you never waste money on faulty merchandise.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈnəʊɪŋ kənˈsjuːmə prəˈtek.ʃən lɔːz ɪnˈʃʊəz juː ˈnevə weɪst ˈmʌni ɒn ˈfɒlti ˈmɜːtʃəndaɪs/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Maintain steady pacing and articulate gerund phrases at the start of your sentences.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Respond to the store clerk who is asking about your warranty coverage.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are arguing that your smartphone repair should be free under the one-year warranty.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Clerk: 'I see your phone has water damage, which is not covered by the standard warranty.'
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: That is incorrect because the water damage occurred due to a manufacturing defect in the seal.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðæt ɪz ˌɪkəˈrekt bɪˈkɒz ðə ˈwɔːtə ˈdæmɪdʒ əˈkɜːd djuː tuː ə ˌmænjuˈfæktʃərɪŋ dɪˈfekt ɪn ðə siːl/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Deliver your rebuttal with a polite yet firm tone of voice.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Demand to speak with a supervisor regarding an unresolved customer complaint.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: The customer service representative refuses to grant a replacement for your broken headphones.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Clerk: 'I apologize, but our store policy strictly prohibits cash refunds after fourteen days.'
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: I understand your policy, but under consumer protection law, I insist on speaking with your supervisor.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /aɪ ˌʌndəˈstænd jɔː ˈpɒlɪsi, bʌt ˈʌndə kənˈsjuːmə prəˈtekʃən lɔː, aɪ ɪnˈsɪst ɒn ˈspiːkɪŋ wɪð jɔː ˈsuːpəvaɪzə/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use a clear, authoritative tone without raising your voice angrily.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Explain that the product specifications online did not match the item delivered.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are discussing an online purchase error with an e-commerce support agent.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Agent: 'The item you received matches the SKU number listed on our checkout page.'
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The SKU might match, but the technical specifications listed on your website were completely misleading.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə eɪskjuː maɪt mætʃ, bʌt ðə ˈteknɪkl ˌspesɪfɪˈkeɪʃnz ˈlɪstɪd ɒn jɔː ˈwebsaɪt wɜː kəmˈpliːtli ˈmɪsliːdɪŋ/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Articulate each syllable of specifications distinctly.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Escalate your complaint after multiple failed attempts to repair a household appliance.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are talking to the service manager after your refrigerator broke down for the third time.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Manager: 'We can send another technician next week to inspect the cooling system again.'
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Sending another technician is unacceptable; I am escalating this matter to demand a brand new replacement.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈsendɪŋ əˈnʌðə ˈteknɪʃn ɪz ˌʌnækˈseptəbl; aɪ æm ˈeskəleɪtɪŋ ðɪs ˈmætə tuː dɪˈmɑːnd ə brænd njuː rɪˈpleɪsmənt/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Emphasize key verbs like escalating and demand to show seriousness.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Read aloud the sentence featuring the target vocabulary word 'entitled'.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Pronounce the sentence clearly focusing on the word entitled.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: As a regular customer, I am fully entitled to a warranty claim for this faulty device.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /æz ə ˈregjʊlə ˈkʌstəmə, aɪ æm ˈfʊli ɪnˈtaɪtld tuː ə ˈwɒrənti kleɪm fɔː ðɪs ˈfɒlti dɪˈvaɪs/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Focus on the correct pronunciation of the schwa sounds and the /t/ plosives.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Read aloud the conditional sentence structure used for constructive complaints.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Read the conditional sentence with correct grammatical pauses.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: If the store refuses my refund, I will report them to the consumer protection bureau.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ɪf ðə stɔː rɪˈfjuːzɪz maɪ ˈriːfʌnd, aɪ wɪl rɪˈpɔːt ðem tuː ðə kənˈsjuːmə prəˈtekʃən ˈbjʊərəʊ/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Pause slightly at the comma between the if clause and the main clause.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Practice syllable stress placement in multi-syllable consumer vocabulary.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Say these three words with correct stress: defective, escalation, specification.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The defective product led to an immediate escalation regarding its technical specification.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə dɪˈfektɪv ˈprɒdʌkt led tuː ən ɪˈmiːdiət ˌeskəˈleɪʃn rɪˈgɑːdɪŋ ɪts ˈteknɪkl ˌspesɪfɪˈkeɪʃn/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Ensure the primary stress in escalation and specification is prominent.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Practice rising and falling intonation when stating facts versus asking for manager help.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Read this statement using a falling tone for facts and a rising tone for the question.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: This appliance is completely faulty. May I speak with your supervisor right away?
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðɪs əˈplaɪəns ɪz kəmˈpliːtli ˈfɒlti. meɪ aɪ spiːk wɪð jɔː ˈsuːpəvaɪzə raɪt əˈweɪ/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Lower your pitch at the end of the first sentence and raise it slightly on the question.
